newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weaker, meets resistance.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weaker, meets resistance.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended weaker on Thursday after rising above the crucial 19,000 point level and meeting heavy resistance, dealers said.
After trading to a low of 18,835, the benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract recovered to 19,030, before falling off its perch in a wave of institutional selling, they said.
"Some big house took profit and knocked the index back down below 19,000 points," a Japanese commission house dealer said.
The March contract ended at 18,960 points on 15,000 lots.
Initial negative sentiment on the back of a retreat in U.S. stocks was viewed as a temporary factor.
But the market mostly shrugged off Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning that U.S. short-term interest rates might head higher to keep inflation in check.
"It's a setback but not for long. Funds are still in the buying mode," another commission house broker said.
The March Nikkei was seen trapped within resistance at 19,300 and 18,750 support, but with gains tempered by recent yen strength against the dollar in currency markets.
The Taiwan index saw record volumes on broad institutional demand. March ended up at 323.4 points on 1,026 lots.
